Lay another plan's rows under a table's

Source: R/plan_append.R
plan_append.Rd

plan_append() builds one table from two sources: the rows of .plan (the parent: say, a listing of each subject's concentrations) and under them the rows of part (the child: their summary statistics), on the same columns. Each is an ordinary plan, run to its table on its own; the tables are stacked before the pages are cut, so a page holds every part's rows of its group. The whole table's settings — header, widths, pages, style, titles — are the parent's, written before or after plan_append().

Usage

plan_append(.plan, part, name = NULL, absent = c("error", "skip"))

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan(): the parent, whose column axis and header the table has.

part

Another table_plan(): its rows go under the rows of .plan. Several plan_append() calls stack their parts in the order written. The part's plan says how its own rows are made and nothing about the whole table (see Parts below).

name

The part's name, for its messages and for plan_layers(): "part2", "part3", ... by default (the parent is "part1"). One non-empty string, not already taken.

absent

What a page group (a value of plan_paginate_rows(page_by = )) the part has no rows for does: "error" (default: a report is not defined by a group that is missing), or "skip" (that page has no rows of this part).

Value

The plan, with one more layer. plan_apply() of it gives the stacked table, with a .part column naming each row's part.

Details

A listing cannot be appended to: a plan that carries plan_listing() stops here, as the parent or as a part, because a listing's columns are the records' own, while the stacked parts are a label and value columns. To show a listing with a summary, make them separate contents of the document: rtf_tables() for the listing, then rtf_tables() for the summary with page_break = FALSE (see the article "Several contents on one page").

Parts

Each plan_append() call adds a part of its own, below the ones added before it; a later call does not replace an earlier one.

plan_append(part) lays another plan's rows under this plan's. The first plan (the parent) is an ordinary table with its column axis and header; a part (the child) is an ordinary plan too, written as any table is, and may carry only the verbs that make its rows: plan_cells(), plan_digits(), plan_labels(), plan_levels() of its row keys, plan_stub(), plan_row_group(), plan_filter(), plan_sort(), plan_nest(), plan_total(), plan_compare(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_hide(), plan_empty(), plan_cell_style() with a condition, and plan_blanks(first =, last =) (a blank row above or below its own rows). Its cols key is the parent's (or left out).

The whole table's settings are the parent's, written anywhere in the parent, before or after plan_append(), the later of two winning as always: the column order (plan_levels() of the column key), the header (plan_col_header()), the widths and decimal split (plan_columns()), the pages (plan_paginate_rows(), plan_paginate_cols()), the blank rows between parts (plan_blanks(where = "between_parts"), and first / last at the table's top and bottom), the style (plan_style()), titles, footnotes and the steps after. A part that carries one of them stops.

What a part does not say, it takes from the parent, key by key: the cell templates, the digits, the labels, the levels of its row keys, the stub fold; what it says itself wins. The empty-cell text is each part's own (plan_cells(na = ), empty by default): the parent's is no statistic's. Its row keys and label are folded into one label column (the parent's plan_stub(name =, indent =)), so every part ends as [page keys] [label] [value columns]: a constant row key (rows = c(block = ~ "Summary Statistics")) is the heading row above its rows, as in any table, and stays empty. Columns a part does not have, and cells it has no value for, print its own empty-cell text.

The parts are stacked before the pages are cut: a page of page_by value X holds the parent's rows of X, then each part's rows of X, matched by value. A blank row between the parts (plan_blanks(where = "between_parts")) is a row of the stack, so it takes a place in max_rows, and a group cut by a page break is continued on the next page by its heading row with cont_label. Every part's data must have the page_by columns (it is not written to every page by default); a value the parent has and a part has not stops, unless that part says absent = "skip"; a value only a part has makes no page.

A part run on its own (plan_apply(part, "table")) is the same rows for every group at once, with only what it says itself: that is the whole difference from the part in the table.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

# Invented concentrations: three subjects, three time points; S-02's
# 4 h sample is below the limit of quantitation (NA)
conc <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = rep(c("S-01", "S-02", "S-03"), each = 3),
  ATPT    = rep(c("1 h", "2 h", "4 h"), 3),
  AVAL    = c(12.1, 8.4, 3.2, 10.5, 7.9, NA, 14.0, 9.6, 4.1))
listing <- table_plan(conc, cols = "ATPT", rows = c(subject = ~ "{USUBJID}"),
                      value = "AVAL") |>
  plan_cells("{value:.1f}", na = "BLQ")

# Their summary, one row a statistic, under one heading row
smry <- data.frame(
  ATPT      = rep(c("1 h", "2 h", "4 h"), each = 2),
  variable  = "AVAL", .label = NA, .kind = "continuous",
  stat_name = c("N", "mean"),
  stat      = c(3, 12.20, 3, 8.633, 2, 3.65))
summary <- table_plan(smry, cols = "ATPT", rows = c(block = ~ "Summary")) |>
  plan_cells(c(N = "{N:.0f}", Mean = "{mean:.2f}"))

# Minimal: the summary's rows under the listing's
listing |> plan_append(summary) |> plan_apply("table")
#>      label   1 h  2 h  4 h .part
#> 1     S-01  12.1  8.4  3.2 part1
#> 2     S-02  10.5  7.9  BLQ part1
#> 3     S-03  14.0  9.6  4.1 part1
#> 4  Summary                 part2
#> 5        N     3    3    2 part2
#> 6     Mean 12.20 8.63 3.65 part2

# The whole table's settings are the parent's: a blank row between the
# parts, and one header for both
pages <- listing |>
  plan_append(summary, name = "summary") |>
  plan_blanks(where = "between_parts") |>
  plan_col_header(rtf_col_header(c("Subject", "{col}"))) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#> ───────────────────────────
#> Subject    1 h   2 h   4 h 
#> ───────────────────────────
#> S-01      12.1   8.4   3.2 
#> S-02      10.5   7.9   BLQ 
#> S-03      14.0   9.6   4.1 
#>                            
#> Summary                    
#>     N       3     3     2  
#>     Mean  12.20  8.63  3.65
#> 
#> <rtftable> 7 rows x 4 columns
#>   Columns:    Subject | 1 h | 2 h | 4 h
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#>
